claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 begins in a high-temperature, well-mixed, metastable BCC state.
Local chemical ordering governs the phase evolution of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 during cooling and thermal exposure.
Al diffuses more rapidly than Cr, Co, Fe, and Ni during cooling or intermediate-temperature exposure.
Differential Al diffusion creates localized compositional fluctuations and Al-rich regions.
Al-rich regions act as nucleation sites for ordered secondary phases.
The compositional fluctuations lower the local free energy of an ordered phase.
B2 domains form at the expense of the metastable BCC phase.
Local chemical order in concentrated multi-principal-element solid solutions can vary with processing conditions.
Slow cooling or prolonged annealing will produce more detectable ordered phase, such as B2, than rapid quenching.
Slow-cooled or annealed samples will contain more detectable Al-rich segregation than rapidly quenched samples.
Rapidly quenched samples will retain a more chemically homogeneous BCC phase.
Rapid quenching suppresses the proposed ordering mechanism by limiting atomic mobility.
Thermal exposures at temperatures too low for significant Al mobility will produce minimal or no ordered phase.
A comparison using identical starting compositions while varying cooling rate and annealing provides the proposed experimental control.
An absence of phase-composition and local-ordering differences between slow-cooled or annealed samples and the rapidly quenched baseline would falsify the proposed mechanism.
